sources.claim: PUT is a hypothetical monthly SPX option-writing benchmark. Historical index comparisons are not account fills.
sources.market_period: Article dated 2021-07-20, monthly index history discussed from July 1986.
sources.data_quality: Published index analysis, underlying observations not imported.
sources.bias: Index construction and selected comparison period. SPX cash settlement differs from SPY assignment.
sources.testable_hypothesis: Compare secured-put after-cost outcomes with a declared benchmark on matched periods, including tail loss.

sources.claim: BXM models index ownership plus monthly at-the-money SPX call writing.
sources.market_period: Methodology reviewed 2026-09-30, no performance sample imported.
sources.bias: Index execution and settlement assumptions differ from physical-stock covered calls.
sources.testable_hypothesis: Compare premium, retained upside and whole-chain downside under matched covered-call policies.

sources.claim: BXMD writes a monthly out-of-the-money SPX call with delta nearest 0.30 against index exposure.
sources.market_period: Methodology reviewed 2026-09-30, no performance sample imported.
sources.bias: Benchmark delta and pricing conventions are not a calibrated THETA rule.
sources.testable_hypothesis: Test the premium versus retained-upside tradeoff against ATM writing with identical cost assumptions.

sources.claim: WPUT combines weekly ATM SPX puts with cash collateral held in Treasury bills.
sources.market_period: Methodology reviewed 2026-09-30, no performance sample imported.
sources.data_quality: Primary index construction, not managed episodes.
sources.bias: Weekly index rolls cannot establish the edge of a 2-5 DTE SPY strategy.
sources.testable_hypothesis: Compare matched short and longer expiry policies after costs and assignment/tail burden.

sources.publisher: Carr and Wu, Review of Financial Studies
sources.claim: The paper estimates variance risk premia using synthetic variance swaps and subsequent realized variance.
sources.market_period: 1996-01-04 to 2003-02-28 overall, per-security start/end dates differ.
sources.data_quality: Peer-reviewed empirical method with OptionMetrics observations, raw data not imported.
sources.bias: Historical period and instrument selection. Variance is not volatility. Future realized variance is a label, never an entry feature.
sources.testable_hypothesis: Evaluate PIT implied-versus-forecast variance evidence against future realized-variance labels out of sample.

sources.claim: A practitioner comparison uses 45-DTE SPY strangles with expiry, 50-percent profit and 21-DTE exits.
sources.market_period: Published 2024-07-01. Exact sample dates are not specified in the retrieved text.
sources.data_quality: Practitioner summary, raw trades and complete reproduction inputs unavailable.
sources.bias: Commercial source, strangles differ from CSPs, execution assumptions require independent validation.
sources.testable_hypothesis: Run the existing profit/time challengers on the same THETA paths without favoring either management hypothesis in advance.

sources.claim: Cash-secured puts reserve purchase funds and retain substantial stock downside after assignment.
sources.bias: Strategy suitability and acquisition preference are not implied by ability to collateralize.
sources.testable_hypothesis: Separate assignment capacity from economic preference and preserve full stock downside in lifecycle comparisons.
